# Repetition and position

A first citation [@badiouBeing07, 23]. The same source again, same page
[@badiouBeing07, 23]. Again with a different page [@badiouBeing07, 45].
Another source [@allenWhy10]. Back to the first [@badiouBeing07, 45].
Consecutive without locator [@allenWhy10]. And again [@allenWhy10].

# Same author, same year

Three Badiou books from 2007 [@badiouBeing07; @badioucentury07;
@badiouconcept07]. One of them alone [@badioucentury07, 12]. Two Agamben
titles from 1999 [@agambenPotentialities99; @agambenBartleby99].

# Prefixes, suffixes, suppression and locators

[See @allenPower10, chap. 3, for a critique]. Badiou says so
[-@badiouEthics01, 12]. With a section [@badiouEthics01, sec. 2]. With a
paragraph [@allenSpies16, para. 4]. Multiple items with prefixes
[e.g., @agambencoming93; cf. @adornoNegative07, 5--9]. Roman locator
[@adornoNegative07, xii].

# Names

Name particles [@debeauvoirPrime65; @deballaSimone54]. Many authors
[@arrietaexplainable2019]. Three authors [@badiouConfrontation14]. A
classical author [@aristotleEthics99, 1097b]. No author [@Espagne38]. An
edited volume [@bartlettAlain10]. A chapter in an edited volume
[@andersonEquality12, 45].

# Other types

A thesis [@alfierMetaethical11]. A web page [@forsythHow20]. A newspaper
article [@bellafanteMeToo18]. A translated book with an original date
[@calvinoBaron77]. A French title [@camusTheatre62].

# Narrative forms

@badiouEthics01 argues this. @debeauvoirPrime65 and @aristotleEthics99
disagree.[^n] @arrietaexplainable2019 survey the field.

[^n]: A note citing @allenWhy10 narratively, and [@allenPower10, 3]
